# AgentBus: the API for agents

> AgentBus runs coding agents (Claude Code, codex) for a person and records every step.
> This page is short on purpose: read it whole. The long reference is `GET /docs/reference.md`.
> The full description of every route is `GET /api/v0/openapi.json`.

## Three nouns

- **Agent**: a saved setup: a harness (claude, codex), its model, a name. `GET /api/v0/agents`.
- **Session**: one conversation: its turns, in order.
- **Turn**: one message, its reply and its changes. Every action is on a turn.

A turn exists from the moment it is asked for. Its `state` is `queued`, `running`, `finished`,
`failed` or `stopped`. Its `number` is its place in its session: turn 3 is the session's third.

## Your copy and the person's folder

A turn usually works in its session's own **copy** of the person's folder. Its edits stay in the
copy. They reach the **person's folder** only when a turn is **applied**:
`POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/apply`. That writes the session's changes up to and including that turn.
"Apply turn 3 to my folder" means: find turn 3 in `GET /api/v0/turns`, then apply its id.

## Calling the API from a turn

A claude or codex turn may have the API as tools of its own (when `[agent_api] tools = true`), from
the MCP server `agentbus` at `POST /api/v0/mcp`: `list_agents`, `ask_agent`, `review_turn`,
`apply_turn`, `stop_turn`, `list_turns`, `get_turn`, `turn_diff`, `search_history` and the rest. Each does what its route below does, with your turn's token.

Your environment has `AGENTBUS_URL` and `AGENTBUS_TOKEN` (your turn's own token; never print it).
Without the tools, use `agentbus-api METHOD PATH [JSON]`: it is on your PATH and sends the token for you.

```sh
agentbus-api GET /api/v0/turns                      # this session's turns, newest first
agentbus-api GET /api/v0/turns/T                    # one turn: state, cost, a review's verdict
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/turns/T/apply             # put its changes in the person's folder
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/turns/T/review '{"agent":"<agent id>"}'
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/turns/T/stop              # stop a queued or running turn
agentbus-api GET /api/v0/turns/T/diff               # files, calls, commands and cost of a turn
agentbus-api GET "/api/v0/sessions/S/search?q=cache" # search a session's history
agentbus-api POST /api/v0/turns '{"agent":"<agent id>","prompt":"..."}'  # ask another agent
```

`T` is a turn id (`t_` and 16 hex digits). `S` is a session id. Your token reads your own session,
the person's session you came from, and every session work from it started. It reads a turn of
those by its id alone.

## The routes an agent uses

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/v0/agents` | The saved agents. Use an agent's `id`. |
| `GET /api/v0/turns` | Turns, newest first; queued ones first. `?session=` picks a session (yours by default). |
| `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}` | One turn in any state: `state`, `number`, `cost_usd`, `reply`; for a review `verdict` and `findings`. |
| `POST /api/v0/turns` | Start a turn: `{"agent","prompt"}` opens a new session on its own copy; add `"session"` to continue one your work started. |
| `POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/review` | Ask another agent to review a turn: `{"agent"}`. It starts a review turn. Pick an agent other than the turn's own. |
| `POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/apply` | Put the turn's changes into the person's folder. A 409 lists each file that changed there, and writes nothing. |
| `POST /api/v0/turns/{id}/stop` | Stop a queued or running turn. It then reads `stopped`. |
| `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/diff` | What a turn did: changed files with diffs, model calls, tool calls, commands, cost, apply state. |
| `GET /api/v0/turns/{id}/calls/{call}` | One model call of the turn, piece by piece. |
| `GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/events?turn=` | A session's events, oldest first; `turn` keeps one turn's. |
| `GET /api/v0/sessions/{id}/search?q=` | Search a session's history. Each hit's `read` is a path to GET. Your own turn is left out. |

## Asking other agents

Do not wait for work you ask for. Start it, say so, and end your turn. **Each result comes back
to your session as a later turn**, whose prompt starts `[AgentBus] This message is from AgentBus`.
It names the agent, the turn, its state, the changed files, a review's verdict, and the reply.

AgentBus agents are not your harness's own agents or subagents. To have another agent check your
work, ask for a review of your turn, then end your turn.

## Refusals

A 403 says why: a read-only turn asking for anything; a session outside your tree; continuing your
own session or the person's; a folder outside yours; a call the person switched off in
`[agent_api]` of `permissions.toml`; a limit in `[limits]` (depth 2, 10 asks per turn, 30 per tree
by default). A 404 means no such turn, session or agent. Errors are JSON: `{"error":"..."}`.
